The Davies Sisters｜印象派转向与战时收藏未作答笔记填空 / 事实判断 TFNG · 3 段 · 268 词 · 4 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 18 页

Q5–6：Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage. Q10–11：TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN。

原文第5段However, it was only a few years before their collecting took a new direction and they turned to the work of the French Impressionists***. We know that Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision, and we know also that they would have seen examples on their various trips to Paris. Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet. Over the next 12 years, the sisters amassed the bulk of their Impressionist collection, including six further works by Monet, two more by Manet, and three by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne.

原文第6段The First World War (1914-1918) played a part in the development of the sisters' collection. Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area. Later in the conflict, both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes, in northern France; Gwendoline in 1916, followed by Margaret in 1917.

原文第7段It was tedious and distressing work, which would have a permanent effect on Gwendoline's health. Yet on one of numerous trips to nearby Paris, she visited the Bernheim-Jeune Gallery. Here she acquired two works by Cézanne - Provençal Landscape and The François Zola Dam. The paintings were shipped directly to Bath, England, where they became the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain.

*** Impressionist: an artist with a style of painting that developed in France in the late 1800s by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne

原页文字提示：脚注引文保留原页；其后半句涉及 Renoir 作品，属于来源编辑瑕疵，不要把整条脚注当作英语完整定义范例。这里的 Impressionist 指印象派画家。

5. the first Impressionist paintings they bought showed places in 5 __________

6. they worked in a 6 __________ for soldiers in France

10. Hugh Blaker opposed the Davies sisters' decision to buy art by French Impressionists.

11. The exhibition of Cézanne paintings at the Bath gallery was very popular with the public.

对照答案，回到证据

第 5 题 · Venice

题干问画中的地点，不是买画地点；Paris是干扰信息。

their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice

第 6 题 · canteen

soldiers对应troops；a后填地点canteen，不能答城市Troyes。

both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes

第 10 题 · FALSE

champion与had a hand in说明支持并参与，和opposed相反，属于明确反证。

Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision

第 11 题 · NOT GIVEN

原文只确认首次公开展出，没有观众反响或人数。全文也未提供其受欢迎程度；first与popular不可互换。

the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

姐妹的收藏逐渐转向法国印象派。文章承认影响因素存在，却没有把转向归结为一个已确定的原因；随后把战争中的救助、志愿服务和购画经历交织起来，展示私人行动如何最终进入公共文化生活。

原文第5段

However, it was only a few years before their collecting took a new direction and they turned to the work of the French Impressionists***. We know that Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision, and we know also that they would have seen examples on their various trips to Paris. Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet. Over the next 12 years, the sisters amassed the bulk of their Impressionist collection, including six further works by Monet, two more by Manet, and three by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne.

收藏方向改变后，姐妹开始购入法国印象派作品。支持当代法国艺术的Hugh Blaker参与了这个决定，她们在巴黎旅行时也应当接触过相关作品，但作者没有断言某一个因素就是决定性原因。1912年她们购入莫奈的威尼斯风景，之后12年形成了印象派收藏的主体。the bulk强调大部分藏品在这一时期积累。

原文第6段

The First World War (1914-1918) played a part in the development of the sisters' collection. Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area. Later in the conflict, both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes, in northern France; Gwendoline in 1916, followed by Margaret in 1917.

第一次世界大战也影响了她们的收藏经历。她们起初出钱帮助被占领比利时的艺术家安全来到威尔士，这既出于人道关怀，也带有发展当地艺术家社群的愿望。后来两人先后到法国为部队食堂做志愿服务。本段把文化理想放在战争救助的现实行动中，而不是只讲艺术市场。

原文第7段

It was tedious and distressing work, which would have a permanent effect on Gwendoline's health. Yet on one of numerous trips to nearby Paris, she visited the Bernheim-Jeune Gallery. Here she acquired two works by Cézanne - Provençal Landscape and The François Zola Dam. The paintings were shipped directly to Bath, England, where they became the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain.

食堂工作单调又令人痛苦，并对格温多琳的健康产生了持久影响。即使如此，她仍在赴巴黎期间参观画廊并购买塞尚的两幅画。这些作品被直接运往英国巴斯，成为英国公共画廊首次展出的塞尚作品。最后一句将个人购藏的故事转向公众能够接触艺术的变化。

词语与搭配

took a new direction

转向新的方向

主语可以是事业、研究或活动的发展；这里的collecting指持续的收藏实践发生变化。

had a hand in the decision

参与或影响了这个决定

have a hand in不表示独自决定；文中同时承认旅行见闻等可能影响。

a vibrant artists' community

一个充满活力的艺术家社群

vibrant强调活跃、有创造力；artists'是复数所有格，community指艺术家相互联系形成的群体，不只是建筑或展馆。

go on display in a public gallery

开始在公共画廊展出

go on display强调从未展出到展出的状态变化，public gallery使私人收藏与公共接触联系起来。

句子精读

Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet.

无论这一变化的确切原因是什么，她们于1912年10月首次购入的印象派作品，都是法国画家克洛德·莫奈描绘威尼斯的风景画。

Whatever the precise reason是省略了may have been一类成分的让步结构，表示不论原因如何。主干是their first purchases were scenes of Venice；made in October 1912是过去分词短语，补充购入时间；by...说明作者。this change指收藏转向印象派，日期、描绘对象与作者属于不同层面的信息。

Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area.

她们最初对战时行动的回应，是资助艺术家从被占领的比利时安全前往威尔士；这是一项人道行动，同时也寄托着在当地建立活跃艺术家社群的希望。

主干是Their initial response was to finance...，不定式说明具体行动。from...to...标明迁移起止地。as a humanitarian act与with the hope of...并列说明两层动机，but also在这里补充文化愿景而非否定人道目的。the area指威尔士当地；hope表明愿望，不能直接当成已经实现的结果。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

a vibrant artists' community

一个充满活力的艺术家社群

适合与support、sustain、help build搭配，讨论实体文化空间如何为创作者提供交流和演出机会。这里借用表达描述一种可能作用，不把文中救助艺术家的历史直接当成剧院效果的证据。

用于写作：题目要求讨论剧院和影院的经济、文化价值；此表达适合展开剧院支持当地艺术生产和创作者交流的文化作用。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

The Davies Sisters｜收藏停止与文化遗产未作答笔记填空 / 事实判断 TFNG · 3 段 · 238 词 · 3 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 18 页

Q7：Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage. Q12–13：TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN。

原文第8段Commentators have often described the sisters as unlikely pioneer collectors. Much is made of their isolation in rural Wales and the fact that they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners. Yet they didn't feel obliged to follow fashionable tastes and were free to pursue their own preferences. Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.

原文第9段By the early 1920s, Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War. Her philanthropic pursuits then became focused almost exclusively on social causes and the development of the sisters' home at Gregynog Hall into a conference center and venue for the Gregynog Festival of Music and Poetry. Gwendoline made her final art purchase in March 1926. Margaret also stopped collecting around this time, but started again in the 1930s acquiring, on a relatively small scale, work by contemporary British artists.

原文第10段The sisters collected French Impressionist paintings at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike. The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists. In collecting paintings that they loved, the sisters created a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy for the people of Wales and beyond.

7. were not considered typical collectors – they lived in isolation in the countryside and did not have any 7 __________ who were artists

12. The impact of the First World War encouraged Gwendoline to reconsider her interest in collecting art.

13. The Davies sisters bought French Impressionist art during a period when very few people were doing so.

对照答案，回到证据

第 7 题 · friends

题干把make friends改为have friends；any后用复数friends，不是advisers。

they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners

第 12 题 · TRUE

战后贫困与动荡使她不安，随后慈善转向社会事业并停止购买，是reconsider的具体证据链。

Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War

第 13 题 · TRUE

ignored by individuals and institutions同时覆盖个人与机构，与very few people were doing so同义。

at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这部分先重新解释姐妹看似偏离艺术圈的生活方式，再说明战争造成的社会问题如何改变她们的支出重点，最后评价收藏留下的公共文化遗产。独立品味、社会责任与文化贡献在结尾汇合。

原文第8段

Commentators have often described the sisters as unlikely pioneer collectors. Much is made of their isolation in rural Wales and the fact that they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners. Yet they didn't feel obliged to follow fashionable tastes and were free to pursue their own preferences. Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.

评论者常把姐妹描述为出人意料的收藏先驱，因为她们住在威尔士乡间，也不与艺术家或画廊主人交朋友。作者随后补充另一面：远离潮流压力使她们能够追随自己的品味。她们仍依赖可信顾问，经常到伦敦和巴黎，也让人把画送到家里考虑，因此地理上的偏远不等于缺少接触作品的机会。

原文第9段

By the early 1920s, Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War. Her philanthropic pursuits then became focused almost exclusively on social causes and the development of the sisters' home at Gregynog Hall into a conference center and venue for the Gregynog Festival of Music and Poetry. Gwendoline made her final art purchase in March 1926. Margaret also stopped collecting around this time, but started again in the 1930s acquiring, on a relatively small scale, work by contemporary British artists.

到1920年代初，战争遗留的贫困和社会动荡使格温多琳对继续购画越来越不安。她把精力几乎完全转向社会事业，并将家宅发展为会议及音乐诗歌节场所，1926年作了最后一次购画。玛格丽特也在大致同期停止收藏，却在1930年代恢复小规模购买当代英国作品。两人的后续选择有关联，但不能合并为完全相同的人生轨迹。

原文第10段

The sisters collected French Impressionist paintings at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike. The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists. In collecting paintings that they loved, the sisters created a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy for the people of Wales and beyond.

文章把个人经历放回当时的艺术接受环境：姐妹收藏印象派时，个人和机构普遍忽视这类作品。她们的藏品后来分别于1951年和1963年捐给威尔士国家博物馆，包含重要画家的代表作。最后一句评价她们追随个人喜爱的行为产生了超出私人范围的长期文化价值。

词语与搭配

free to pursue their own preferences

能够自由追随自己的喜好

be free to强调不受外部义务或压力束缚；这里与不必追随流行趣味相连，不表示完全不接受建议。

when faced with the poverty and social upheaval

面对贫困和社会动荡时

when faced with是省略主语和be动词的结构，后接所面对的局面；说明价值判断发生变化的社会背景。

on a relatively small scale

以相对较小的规模

scale描述活动的规模，relatively保留比较意味；这里限定玛格丽特后来恢复收藏的程度。

a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy

持久且有意义的文化遗产

legacy是前人行动留给后来者的影响或成果；这里不是遗产金额，而是可被公众持续接触的艺术收藏。

句子精读

Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.

虽然她们依靠一群信赖的顾问，但仍经常前往伦敦和巴黎，也常让人把画送到家中供她们考虑。

Although引出依靠顾问的事实，主句突出她们自己的主动参与。made frequent trips和had paintings sent并列；have something done表示安排别人完成某事，sent是过去分词。for consideration说明送画是为了供她们考察是否购买，而非已经购入。

The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists.

格温多琳和玛格丽特·戴维斯的收藏分别于1951年和1963年捐给威尔士国家博物馆，其中包括法国重要印象派画家的代表作品。

主干是collection contains major examples。donated...是插入的过去分词短语，补充藏品的捐赠去向和时间；respectively将两位姐妹按姓名顺序与两个年份对应。by leading French Impressionists修饰work，leading在这里指具有重要地位，并非位置靠前。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy

持久且有意义的文化遗产

可用于讨论文化活动对未来的贡献，但要写清通过什么机制传承，例如保留地方戏剧、作品或表演传统，不能只用抽象赞美代替解释。

用于写作：直接服务于实体剧院的文化价值：说明现场演出空间如何承载和传递传统，而不只比较观看的便利程度。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

Why we need silence｜漂浮舱的两项实验未作答摘要填空 / 人物／特征匹配 · 3 段 · 311 词 · 5 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 21 页

Q18–21：Complete the summary. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Q24：Match the statement with the correct person A–D.

DResearchers are also seeking to understand what aspects of silent experiences are most beneficial to our health. One of the best-researched is the flotation tank: a lightproof, soundproof tank of salt water in which a person floats as a form of deep relaxation. While some people experience altered perception in the tanks, involving subtle humming sounds and visual effects, these effects are benign and do not detract from the benefits of the experience, says Justin Feinstein, a clinical neuropsychologist. 'When you don't have external sensory stimuli coming in, the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world,' he explains. 'In these tanks, some people can even hear the sound of their eyes blinking,' says Feinstein. 'But it is the ability to focus on the breath that helps people reach a relaxed or meditative state.'

E（第一段）E To further explore flotation tanks as a therapeutic tool, Feinstein and his colleagues recruited 50 people with a variety of conditions related to stress and had them answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session. Participants reported decreases in muscle tension, pain and symptoms of their conditions after a single, 1-hour float, alongside an increase in feelings of relaxation and overall wellbeing.

E（第二段）Less is known about what effects sensory deprivation can have on the brain. To investigate, Feinstein's team had 48 people participate in either three 90-minute float sessions or three 90-minute periods of relaxing on a chair which reclined. Participants had their brains scanned using functional magnetic resonance imaging at the beginning and end of the trial. Float sessions uniquely decreased activity in the default mode network (DMN), a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression. Feinstein says it is an exciting finding, because flotation tanks seem to offer a way of 'resetting' our nervous system to prevent it from getting out of balance.

18. According to Justin Feinstein, flotation tanks allow people to concentrate on their own 18 __________, which helps them relax and enables them to meditate.

19. Feinstein and his colleagues conducted an experiment in which 50 people, who were all suffering from stress and related issues, were given a 19 __________ to complete before and after using a flotation tank.

20. Participants reported a reduction in their symptoms after an hour in the tank, together with signs of relaxation and improved general 20 __________.

21. In another experiment, the researchers had 48 people spend periods of 90 minutes either lying back in a chair or floating in a tank. Brain scans then revealed that those people who had been in a tank had decreased activity in parts of the brain associated with 21 __________.

24. When our body's senses are completely deprived of input, our minds compensate for this by creating the illusion of images and sounds.

  • A Nick Antonio
  • B Justin Feinstein
  • C Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan
  • D Eric Pfeifer

对照答案，回到证据

第 18 题 · breath

concentrate on与focus on同义；不是描述感官幻觉的humming sounds。

the ability to focus on the breath

第 19 题 · questionnaire

50 people唯一锁定第一项实验，before and after对应prior to and following。

answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session

第 20 题 · wellbeing

general对应overall；答案是整体状态wellbeing，不是症状pain。

an increase in feelings of relaxation and overall wellbeing

第 21 题 · depression

associated with对应linked with；48人/90分钟与上一项50人/一小时必须分开。

a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression

第 24 题 · B

D引语来自Feinstein；visual effects与humming sounds对应images and sounds。

the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这一部分围绕漂浮舱提出两个层次的问题：人主观上有什么感受，脑活动发生了什么变化。文章分别介绍问卷与脑扫描研究，并保留科学解释中的不确定性；参与者报告的轻松感不能直接扩大成对所有疾病或所有人的疗效结论。

D

D Researchers are also seeking to understand what aspects of silent experiences are most beneficial to our health. One of the best-researched is the flotation tank: a lightproof, soundproof tank of salt water in which a person floats as a form of deep relaxation. While some people experience altered perception in the tanks, involving subtle humming sounds and visual effects, these effects are benign and do not detract from the benefits of the experience, says Justin Feinstein, a clinical neuropsychologist. 'When you don't have external sensory stimuli coming in, the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world,' he explains. 'In these tanks, some people can even hear the sound of their eyes blinking,' says Feinstein. 'But it is the ability to focus on the breath that helps people reach a relaxed or meditative state.'

漂浮舱通过遮光、隔音和盐水漂浮减少外界感觉输入。有人会听见轻微嗡鸣或出现视觉感受，Feinstein认为这可能是大脑在缺少外界刺激时尝试填补空白。这些现象在他的描述中是良性的；真正帮助进入放松状态的，是把注意力放在呼吸上的能力。本段是在介绍一种体验及专家解释，并非要求读者自行进行治疗。

E（第一段）

E To further explore flotation tanks as a therapeutic tool, Feinstein and his colleagues recruited 50 people with a variety of conditions related to stress and had them answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session. Participants reported decreases in muscle tension, pain and symptoms of their conditions after a single, 1-hour float, alongside an increase in feelings of relaxation and overall wellbeing.

研究团队招募50名有不同压力相关状况的人，在一次漂浮前后填写问卷。参与者报告一小时后肌肉紧张、疼痛和相关症状减少，放松感与整体舒适感提高。这里的信息来自参与者的前后自报；本段没有交代对照条件或长期追踪，因而只宜理解为此次研究中观察到的短时体验变化。

E（第二段）

Less is known about what effects sensory deprivation can have on the brain. To investigate, Feinstein's team had 48 people participate in either three 90-minute float sessions or three 90-minute periods of relaxing on a chair which reclined. Participants had their brains scanned using functional magnetic resonance imaging at the beginning and end of the trial. Float sessions uniquely decreased activity in the default mode network (DMN), a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression. Feinstein says it is an exciting finding, because flotation tanks seem to offer a way of 'resetting' our nervous system to prevent it from getting out of balance.

第二项研究改为考察大脑：48人分别接受三次90分钟漂浮或在躺椅上放松，并在研究开始和结束时做功能磁共振扫描。原文报告只有漂浮组出现默认模式网络活动降低，该网络常与抑郁有关。Feinstein把这解释为可能帮助神经系统重获平衡的线索；seem和resetting上的引号提醒读者，这是一种试探性、形象化解释，不等于已经证明能治疗抑郁。

词语与搭配

external sensory stimuli

外界感觉刺激

F（第一段）F Neurobiologist Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan is also an advocate of silence as a therapy. 核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这是一篇书评的开头：作者介绍Bosma如何把糖写成一部全球贸易史和劳动史。甘蔗糖与甜菜糖、进口来源的变化、大种植园与小农生产相互补充，使糖的历史不再只剩单一地区或单一劳动制度。

原文第1段

Ulbe Bosma's The World of Sugar is a genuinely global history. Bosma discusses all the sugar growing places of the world, beginning with Cuba and Java, the largest exporters of the early 20th century. But this is a history not just of cane sugar but also of beet sugar, an equally important form of traded sugar over the last hundred years. Beet sugar is grown mainly in Europe and the United States. It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

书评首先评价这是一部真正具有全球范围的糖史，既讨论古巴和爪哇等甘蔗糖出口地，也把欧洲、美国的甜菜糖纳入。随后指出补贴与人为压低的价格会影响世界市场，威胁甘蔗糖生产者的生计。It指甜菜糖这一行业和产品，不能理解为世界上所有糖生产都采用同一制度。

原文第2段

Bosma's discussion of the sugar market in Britain gives a sense of the book's range. The sweet-toothed British first bought cane sugar from their own slavery-dependent colonial plantations. Following the abolition of slavery in the British Empire, cane sugar was imported to Britain from places which retained the practice, such as Cuba and Brazil. Towards the end of the 19th century, the British started to import beet sugar from continental Europe. Only in the 20th century was there a move to develop a national beet sugar industry.

英国市场的进口变化展示了全书的跨度：先从依赖奴役劳动的本国殖民种植园购买甘蔗糖，废奴后仍从保留奴隶制的古巴、巴西等地进口，19世纪末开始进口欧洲甜菜糖，20世纪才发展本国甜菜糖业。这段揭示，某国法律改变与商品供应链中的劳动制度变化并不一定同步。

原文第3段

The book provides a global labour history, investigating the wide range of labour regimes associated with growing sugar. Contrary to popular belief, cane sugar production was never just restricted to large, dedicated plantations owned by rich men. For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

作者转向劳动组织的多样性，纠正甘蔗糖始终只由富人拥有的大型专门种植园生产这一单一想象。爪哇的小农曾以高度劳动密集的方式同时种甘蔗和水稻，是这种多样性的一个实例。not just restricted强调不只存在大种植园，并没有否认大种植园的重要历史。

词语与搭配

sold at artificially low prices

以人为压低的价格出售

artificially在这里指价格受到补贴等外部干预，不是说产品是假货；at引出出售价格。

threatening the livelihood of

威胁……的生计

livelihood指赖以谋生的方式和收入基础；此处现在分词说明低价竞争带来的影响。

Following the abolition of slavery

在奴隶制废除之后

following相当于after，标记时间关系；它本身不保证其他国家或供应链也同时发生同样变化。

Contrary to popular belief

与普遍看法相反

用于引入与常见理解不一致的事实，后面需要具体内容或例证支持，不能只把自己的意见写成事实纠正。

an extraordinarily labour-intensive way

一种极为依赖大量劳动投入的方式

labour-intensive描述生产对劳动投入的依赖程度，与单纯技术先进或落后不是同一个概念。

句子精读

It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

甜菜糖还获得了巨额补贴，并在世界市场上以人为压低的价格出售，威胁着甘蔗糖生产者的生计。

It承接上句的beet sugar；has been统领subsidised和sold两个被动分词。at引出价格，on world markets说明交易范围。末尾threatening...是补充结果的现在分词短语，说明受影响的是甘蔗糖生产者，而非把两种糖当成同一种生产群体。

For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

例如，在20世纪初的重要食糖出口地爪哇，小农以极其劳动密集的方式，把甘蔗与水稻一起种植。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

threatening the livelihood of

威胁……的生计

适合用于描述资源衰退或不公平竞争怎样影响依赖某产业谋生的人。可以作为结果分词短语，但要让前面的原因具体可理解。

Do animals dream?｜跨物种睡眠研究未作答表格填空 · 4 段 · 355 词 · 5 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 39 页

Complete the table below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. 各行研究结果与评论合并为可输入题面，物种及原空号保留。

原文第1段Studies using electrodes attached to the heads of sleepers have shown that when we sleep, we do so in two ways that alternate throughout the night. The first is rapid eye movement (REM) or active sleep. During this stage our eyes move, even though our eyelids are closed. Our muscles also twitch slightly, though they are largely paralysed so we don't hurt ourselves. In contrast, we also engage in non-REM sleep, during which we barely move at all. Most dream states, and certainly those with the most vivid dreams, happen during REM sleep.

原文第2段There's some evidence that other mammals may also dream. For example, researchers compared the brain patterns of rats running through a maze when awake with their brain patterns during REM sleep. They found the patterns were very similar and concluded that the sleeping rats were dreaming about going through the maze.

原文第3段But finding evidence of dreaming in non-mammals has proved more difficult. Their brains are very different from those of humans, and it can often be difficult to record their activity while they are sleeping. Recently, however, researchers succeeded in recording brain activity in sleeping pigeons. As in mammals, the recordings revealed both REM and non-REM sleep. Intriguingly, REM sleep activity was high in brain regions involved in processing visual information, especially images related to physical activities such as flying, which suggests that this may possibly be what the pigeons were dreaming about.

原文第4段That said, dreaming and REM sleep are unlikely to be universal in the animal kingdom. For example, sponges don't have brains, so they lack the machinery for dreaming. There are also some animals with unusual sleep patterns. These include whales and dolphins, which do not shut down their entire brain when they sleep, but only half of it, keeping the rest awake. They also show no sign of REM sleep, suggesting that they may only experience non-REM dreams, which are less vivid. This is surprising because we tend to think of whales and dolphins as having complex inner lives. It's thought that they don't experience REM sleep because during REM sleep animals are more vulnerable to extremes of temperature.

2. Pigeons: when sleeping, pigeons displayed activity in parts of the brain that deal with 2 __________ input; may have been dreaming of flying

3. Whales and dolphins: still have 3 __________ their brain awake when they sleep

4. Whales and dolphins: don't experience REM sleep, as this could affect their sensitivity to 4 __________

5. Whales and dolphins: their dreams are probably not very 5 __________

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

作者从人类的两种睡眠状态出发，逐步追问其他动物是否也做梦。脑活动记录提供了跨物种比较的线索，但动物无法直接报告梦境，所以观察到的睡眠特征与对主观体验的推测始终需要区分。

原文第1段

Studies using electrodes attached to the heads of sleepers have shown that when we sleep, we do so in two ways that alternate throughout the night. The first is rapid eye movement (REM) or active sleep. During this stage our eyes move, even though our eyelids are closed. Our muscles also twitch slightly, though they are largely paralysed so we don't hurt ourselves. In contrast, we also engage in non-REM sleep, during which we barely move at all. Most dream states, and certainly those with the most vivid dreams, happen during REM sleep.

电极研究表明，人的睡眠在快速眼动与非快速眼动状态之间交替。快速眼动时眼球活动、肌肉可能轻微抽动，但大部分肌肉受到抑制；非快速眼动时身体几乎不动。多数梦境，尤其生动的梦，与快速眼动睡眠相连。本段提供后文比较动物的基础，但most没有把全部梦境都限定在一种状态。

原文第2段

There's some evidence that other mammals may also dream. For example, researchers compared the brain patterns of rats running through a maze when awake with their brain patterns during REM sleep. They found the patterns were very similar and concluded that the sleeping rats were dreaming about going through the maze.

研究者比较老鼠清醒走迷宫时和快速眼动睡眠中的脑活动，发现两者相似，因此推测老鼠可能在梦中重现走迷宫的经历。这里先有脑活动模式的观察，再有对梦内容的解释；开头some evidence和may保留了动物内在体验无法直接验证的限制。

原文第3段

But finding evidence of dreaming in non-mammals has proved more difficult. Their brains are very different from those of humans, and it can often be difficult to record their activity while they are sleeping. Recently, however, researchers succeeded in recording brain activity in sleeping pigeons. As in mammals, the recordings revealed both REM and non-REM sleep. Intriguingly, REM sleep activity was high in brain regions involved in processing visual information, especially images related to physical activities such as flying, which suggests that this may possibly be what the pigeons were dreaming about.

研究非哺乳动物更困难，因为脑结构不同，睡眠中的脑活动也更难记录。鸽子的记录显示两类睡眠状态，并且快速眼动时视觉信息处理区域较活跃，特别涉及飞行等身体活动的影像。作者因此提出可能与相应梦境有关，但suggests、may和possibly层层保留推测，不能直接写成研究人员看到了鸽子的梦。

原文第4段

That said, dreaming and REM sleep are unlikely to be universal in the animal kingdom. For example, sponges don't have brains, so they lack the machinery for dreaming. There are also some animals with unusual sleep patterns. These include whales and dolphins, which do not shut down their entire brain when they sleep, but only half of it, keeping the rest awake. They also show no sign of REM sleep, suggesting that they may only experience non-REM dreams, which are less vivid. This is surprising because we tend to think of whales and dolphins as having complex inner lives. It's thought that they don't experience REM sleep because during REM sleep animals are more vulnerable to extremes of temperature.

That said转向适用范围：梦和快速眼动不太可能遍布所有动物。海绵没有大脑；鲸与海豚只让半侧大脑进入睡眠，文中说它们没有快速眼动睡眠迹象，进而推测可能只有较不生动的非快速眼动梦。末句以It's thought提出一种温度脆弱性的解释，属于学术推测，不是确定且唯一的原因。
